title: EGY-18 · The educated Egyptian: present, discuss, converse

blocks.text: EGY-18 · The educated Egyptian: present, discuss, converse
Lesson overview

In EGY-17 you have learned to recognize the educated Egyptian: the Egyptian grammar with the vocabulary of fuṣḥā, who use educated people when talking about work, society or current affairs. In this unit learn how to use it: present a topic in three-five minutes, discuss and disagree nicely at a meeting, answer audience questions, hold a free conversation of 15 minutes. You also learn to switch from one register to another: the same Šarīf that in a podcast would saylaʾ w-ēh- In a meeting says "zayy" but ḥaḍratkum šayfīn». It is the last unit of the Egyptian track of B2: In the end you find the Egyptian skills profile to be checked with the tutor. Eight weeks, in parallel with the end of B2-15, B2-16, the Test B2.3 and B2-17.

rows: EGY-11 EGY-17 (in particular EGY-12, talk show, and EGY-17, the educated Egyptian)
12–13 hours · eight weeks (weeks) 219–226), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, an Egyptian tutor, a recorder (also the phone), interviews and authentic Egyptian conferences chosen by the tutor
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. reword in Egyptian read a content said in Egyptian daily;
2. submit an argument in three to five minutes with a clear structure and the appropriate formulas;
3. expressing agreement, reservations and disagreement with politeness, addressing those who listen to ḥaḍritak, ḥaḍratkum;
4. answer public questions and close an intervention;
5. support a 15-minute free conversation, using strategies not to block you.
Eight-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

Three tips. Always announce the plan (the audience knows where you are); use a concrete example for each point; repeat the conclusion in a sentence. A four-minute presentation corresponds to about 400–450 words: prepare a playlist, not a text to read.

5. Pronunciation

The words translated into the Egyptian mouth. The words of fuṣḥā they are pronounced with the Egyptian sounds: ⁧ث⁩ → s o t (ṯaqāfa → saqāfa; ṯalāṯa → talāta), ⁧ذ⁩ → z o d (ḏakiyy → zaki), ⁧ظ⁩ → ẓ (ẓurūf), ⁧ج⁩ → g (ǧāmiʿa → gamʿa). The ⁧ق⁩ , on the other hand, in the translated words is often pronounced q (il-qanūn, il-qaḍiyya, il-iqtiṣād), while in everyday words it becomes ʾ (ʾalb, ʾahwa). 7. The free conversation
In a long conversation the problem is not grammar, but not getting stuck. Five strategies:

maʿlišš, mumkin tiʿīd? · bi-r-rāḥa šwayya, law samaḥt
yaʿni ḥaḍritak ʾaṣdak Inn...? · yaʿni Il-fikra inn...?
bypass the word that is missing
il-ḥāga ili binistaʿmilha ʿašān... · zayy... bass... · bititʾāl izzāy bi-l-maṣri?

blocks.text: re-launch w-inta / w-ḥaḍritak, ēh raʾyak? · ḥaṣal maʿāk ḥāga zayy kida?

The word that's missing. If you don't know a word, describe it:il-ḥāga ili binistaʿmilha ʿašān nifṭaḥ il-ʿilab” (= “the can opener”). Whoever listens to you will almost always suggest it: repeat it immediately and use it. It's the quickest way to learn new vocabulary in conversation.

B · Formules (4 points). What do you say: 7. to open a presentation? · 8. to announce the plan? · 9. to express a reservation? · 10. to close and open questions? C · Submission and applications (10 points). Present to the tutor in three minutes a theme chosen by him among three proposals (ten minutes of preparation, just playlist), then answer two questions.
